name: Atlántico
summary_text: Caribe Afirmativo's 2025 annual report issues a specific, named warning of "increasing violence against LGBTIQ+ people in the Atlántico department," and quantifies it: 54 cases of intrafamily violence, 41 sexual offences, 12 discrimination cases, 8 digital-violence cases, 69 threats and 8 lethal-violence cases in the department, with 2 killings of LGBTIQ+ human-rights defenders; the report designates Barranquilla and Soledad as territories at "high" threat level. Barranquilla is the Caribbean-coast hub for trans sex work and the city where the NGO's documentation base operates, giving it both elevated exposure and visibility in monitoring data; the department appears explicitly in the 270-victim national total (+63% on 2024; one killing every 32 hours). Impunity is near-total nationally: 99.8% of threat cases never advanced past the investigation stage. A positive institutional signal is recorded: the department's development plan (and Barranquilla's) commits coordinated action with the prosecutor's office, police and judiciary to strengthen reporting, investigation and prosecution of violent acts against LGBTIQ+ people. Versus the national score (~0.52), Atlántico falls approximately 0.09 lower, justified by the NGO's named escalation warning (not merely inclusion in aggregate counts, but a specific "increase" call-out) and the structural role of Barranquilla's trans sex-work corridor. Versus Antioquia (0.33), Atlántico is higher: its violence is a rising trend flagged by Caribe Afirmativo rather than the decade-deep, impunity-saturated lethality concentration that makes Antioquia "one of the most dangerous" in Colombia. Versus Bolívar (0.44), Atlántico sits marginally lower because its finding is a forward-looking escalation warning tied to a specific urban hub, whereas Bolívar's deviation rests on one targeted killing of a named community leader.

sources.title: Caribe Afirmativo alerta aumento de violencia contra población LGBTIQ+ en Atlántico y Colombia en 2025 – Publimetro Colombia
sources.claim_summary: Metro (Barranquilla edition), 17 May 2026: Caribe Afirmativo's 2025 report "Un sistema que falla" (270 fatal victims nationally, +63% on 2024's 165 homicides, one killing every 32 hours) warns of rising violence including in the Atlántico department - 54 intrafamily-violence cases, 41 sexual offences, 12 discrimination cases, 8 digital-violence cases, 69 threats, 2 homicides of defenders, 8 lethal-violence cases; Barranquilla and Soledad named at "high" threat level; analysis of the departmental and municipal development plans' coordinated actions with prosecutors, police and courts.

sources.title: Colombia enfrenta una crisis estructural de violencia contra personas LGBTIQ+: una persona fue asesinada cada 32 horas en 2025 – Corporación Caribe Afirmativo
sources.claim_summary: Caribe Afirmativo report page (2025 data): structural crisis - one LGBTIQ+ person killed every 32 hours; continuum of violence (discrimination to family violence to sexual violence to threats to homicide to impunity); 1,184 threat victims used as territorial-control mechanisms; 1,531 intrafamily-violence and 628 sexual-violence cases; digital violence (doxxing, identity theft, revenge porn) as escalation catalyst; violence concentrated in major urban centres with expansion into territories with armed actors and illegal economies; 160 information requests to public entities with widespread non-response.
